{{Short description|Construction in algebraic topology}}
In mathematics, specifically in [[algebraic topology]] and [[algebraic geometry]],  an '''inverse image functor''' is a [[Covariance and contravariance of functors|contravariant]] construction of [[Sheaf (mathematics)|sheaves]]; here “contravariant” in the sense given a map <math>f : X \to Y</math>, the inverse image [[functor]] is a functor from the [[Category_(mathematics)|category]] of sheaves on ''Y'' to the category of sheaves on ''X''. The [[direct image functor]] is the primary operation on sheaves, with the simplest definition. The inverse image exhibits some relatively subtle features.
{{Images of sheaves}}

==Definition==
Suppose we are given a sheaf <math>\mathcal{G}</math> on <math>Y</math> and that we want to transport <math>\mathcal{G}</math> to <math>X</math> using a [[Continuous function (topology)|continuous map]] <math>f\colon X\to Y</math>.  

We will call the result the ''inverse image'' or [[pullback (category theory)|pullback]] [[sheaf (mathematics)|sheaf]] <math>f^{-1}\mathcal{G}</math>.  If we try to imitate the [[direct image]] by setting 
:<math>f^{-1}\mathcal{G}(U) = \mathcal{G}(f(U))</math> 
for each open set <math>U</math> of <math>X</math>, we immediately run into a problem: <math>f(U)</math> is not necessarily open.  The best we could do is to approximate it by open sets, and even then we will get a [[presheaf]] and not a sheaf. Consequently, we define <math>f^{-1}\mathcal{G}</math> to be the [[sheaf associated to the presheaf]]:

:<math>U \mapsto \varinjlim_{V\supseteq f(U)}\mathcal{G}(V).</math>
(Here <math>U</math> is an [[Open set|open subset]] of <math>X</math> and the [[colimit]] runs over all open subsets <math>V</math> of <math>Y</math> containing <math>f(U)</math>.)

For example, if <math>f</math> is just the inclusion of a point <math>y</math> of <math>Y</math>, then <math>f^{-1}(\mathcal{F})</math> is just the [[Stalk (sheaf)|stalk]] of <math>\mathcal{F}</math> at this point.

The restriction maps, as well as the [[functoriality]] of the inverse image follows from the [[universal property]] of [[direct limit]]s.

When dealing with [[morphisms]] <math>f\colon X\to Y</math> of [[locally ringed space]]s, for example [[scheme (mathematics)|schemes]] in [[algebraic geometry]], one often works with [[sheaf of modules|sheaves of <math>\mathcal{O}_Y</math>-modules]], where <math>\mathcal{O}_Y</math> is the structure sheaf of <math>Y</math>. Then the functor <math>f^{-1}</math> is inappropriate, because in general it does not even give sheaves of <math>\mathcal{O}_X</math>-modules. In order to remedy this, one defines in this situation for a sheaf of <math>\mathcal O_Y</math>-modules <math>\mathcal G</math> its inverse image  by

:<math>f^*\mathcal G := f^{-1}\mathcal{G} \otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal{O}_Y} \mathcal{O}_X</math>.

== Properties ==

* While <math>f^{-1}</math> is more complicated to define than <math>f_{\ast}</math>, the [[stalk (sheaf)|stalks]] are easier to compute: given a point <math>x \in X</math>, one has <math>(f^{-1}\mathcal{G})_x \cong \mathcal{G}_{f(x)}</math>.
* <math>f^{-1}</math> is an [[exact functor]], as can be seen by the above calculation of the stalks.
* <math>f^*</math> is (in general) only right exact. If <math>f^*</math> is exact, ''f'' is called [[Flat morphism|flat]].
* <math>f^{-1}</math> is the [[adjoint functor|left adjoint]] of the [[direct image functor]] <math>f_{\ast}</math>.  This implies that there are natural unit and counit morphisms <math>\mathcal{G} \rightarrow f_*f^{-1}\mathcal{G}</math> and <math>f^{-1}f_*\mathcal{F} \rightarrow \mathcal{F}</math>. These morphisms yield a natural adjunction correspondence:
:<math>\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf {Sh}(X)}(f^{-1} \mathcal G, \mathcal F ) = \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf {Sh}(Y)}(\mathcal G, f_*\mathcal F)</math>.
However, the morphisms <math>\mathcal{G} \rightarrow f_*f^{-1}\mathcal{G}</math> and <math>f^{-1}f_*\mathcal{F} \rightarrow \mathcal{F}</math> are ''almost never'' isomorphisms. 
For example, if <math>i\colon Z \to Y</math> denotes the inclusion of a [[Closed set|closed subset]], the stalk of <math>i_* i^{-1} \mathcal G</math> at a point <math>y \in Y</math> is canonically isomorphic to <math>\mathcal G_y</math> if <math>y</math> is in <math>Z</math> and <math>0</math> otherwise. A similar adjunction holds for the case of sheaves of modules, replacing <math>i^{-1}</math> by <math>i^*</math>.
